recipes.name: Cabbage Fat-Burning Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can cut green beans, drained
2 (16 ounce) cans whole peeled tomatoes, with liquid
1 (1 ounce) envelope dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Place celery, carrots, onions, cabbage, bell peppers, and green beans in a large soup pot.
Add tomato juice, tomatoes, beef broth, and enough water to cover vegetables; add onion soup mix and stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over medium heat; reduce heat to low and simmer until vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cabbage Fat-Burning Soup
raw_recipe.description: This weight-loss cabbage soup recipe uses tomatoes, bell peppers, carrots, onions, and chopped cabbage to make a filling, fat-free, low-calorie soup.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a cabbage soup that’s loaded with fresh vegetables. It’s fat free, low calorie, and packed full of healthy ingredients: tomatoes, cabbage, carrots, onions, green beans, and bell peppers. A package of onion soup mix adds big flavor to the tomato juice and broth base

review.reviewBody: I would recommend NOT making alterations to this soup because the purpose of the set recipe is to lose weight. I did lose weight when I made this (it was for a vacation), and it tasted great!! I checked with a local hospital, and they said this recipe is used for overweight patients to get them to lose weight rapidly to prepare for surgery. I would recommend this recipe to anyone!

First of all, a minor caveat-- I've never had to diet, since I have a pretty fast metabolism, so I can't really compare this to other diets. BUT... Several years ago, I started a new job and found myself sending out for fast food for lunch every day, eating it at my desk. All of a sudden, my clothes started to... *shrink*. I stepped on the scxale and saw that I'd gained 15 pounds!!! I panicked!

Found this "diet" and decided to try it. The weight just went away! It does get a little boring... But it's tasty and painless; think about adding different spices and/or herbs to the soup to vary it... chili powder, curry, etc. Now, I *did* have to change the way I had lunch once I lost the weight... No more fast food breakfasts and lunches (except for the occasional emergency...), trying to get out and walk a bit a few times a week at lunch... But it did get the weight off and-- with my revamped lunch hour-- kept it off.

I ate this soup for months when the recipe came out years ago. You have to eat nothing else to lose weight....and I did, about 30 lbs.!! I gave the recipe to everyone at work and they all lost weight too. Besides which, it is an excellent soup (not so much for breakfast as we did back then!) but I still like it. I have added chick peas to the recipe for some protein. Also some lean hamburger goes well. Thanks for the memories!

Very good. I used my food processor for most of the chopping, adjusted the seasonings to my personal taste, and simmered for a couple of hours. I froze individual servings and have been bringing it to work for lunch. It's very filling. The only thing I would/will do differently next time is transfer some of the soup to a blender and process until smooth, then add back into the soup for a creamier texture.

I add a few different herbs and spices to each batch to give it an international twist. For example, I add chopped cilantro, a little chili powder, and cumin to give it a Southwestern flavor; some oregano, basil, and fresh garlic for an Italian taste; a little curry powder mixed into the cooking soup and chopped fresh mint leaves for garnish on top when serving to give it a unique Moroccan flavor; shrimp or fish boullion, a little soy sauce, and some fresh bean sprouts, minus the tomatoes for an exotic Oriental sensation; chanterelle mushrooms and a pinch of thyme and rosemary minus the tomatoes for a wonderful French taste. All very yummy! Also on the skim milk day add some non-fat plain yogurt to soup. Also a good tip is to make a banana and milk smoothy on banana and milk day. All these tips help make my 7 days alot easier.

Good base recipe. The following substitutions keep it low calorie. I subbed yellow squash for the carrots and added 1 lb. of fresh green beans instead of the canned. To increase flavor, I added a tablespoon of Better Than Bouillon beef base, a 16 oz. jar of medium salsa, and 4 bay leaves. This made more than 10 quarts and will freeze well.

Yes I made a few changes cuz I had to use what I had on hand. NOTE: USE A VERY LARGE STOCK PAN. For ALL the tomato products that this recipe called for I used 1 can stewed tomatoes and 1 can diced tomatoes, I used a huge can of cento crushed tomatoes then I filled the cento can with water twice to make sure all the veggies were covered. I used 2 cans of drained green beans instead of one. I ADDED 2 LBS OF BROWNED GROUND VENISON AND 1 POUND OF CHOPPED TURKEY KIELBASA BOTH BROWNED & DRAINED OF ANY FAT. I ADDED A HEAPING TBLSP OF MINCED GARLIC AND A HEAPING TBLSP OF ITALIAN SEASONING AND A FLAT TBLSP OF WET RED CRUSHED PEPPER and a sprinkling of salt and black pepper. I included all the other ingredients that this recipe called for which filled my biggest stock pot to the top and I simmered it on low for probably 45 minutes to an hour. It is so YUMMY, 5 STARS, 2 THUMBS UP AND I'VE BEEN EATING THIS FOR 3 DAYS AND HAVE LOST 4 LBS. I'M SO HAPPY. IT'S ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS AND I'M LOSING WEIGHT AND HAVEN'T EXERCISED A BIT BECAUSE I'VE GOT THE FLU & PNEUMONIA RIGHT NOW SO THIS RECIPE IS WORKING GREAT FOR ME PERSONALLY TO LOSE POUNDS. BUT I DON'T EAT ANYTHING ELSE. I DO HAVE A VERY GOOD HEARTY SIZED BOWL WHEN I DO EAT THIS every day and as often as I feel hungry every day which is usually twice a day. It very filling and so tasty! Give it a try, you won't be disappointed. Delish!!!!

As written, this recipe is very high in sodium. I made this soup using low sodium versions of just about everything and it turned out great. I replaced the onion soup mix with a cajun spice mix I found on AR (low sodium). If you are using this as a healthy weight loss option, sodium is an important factor to consider. Thanks for posting!

This is an all-time family favorite... the only difference is we don't use onion soup mix--the chopped onion is sufficient, and only use organic ingredients. Since this is such a huge recipe, I cut it back about half so it fits in my crockpot (takes 5-6 hours). I've never had to add water (except to rinse out the canned tomato jars and tomato juice bottles). I've always used a 32 oz. carton of beef broth and added some pepper. Spices can be added to this "at will" and it'll still be fantastic! This is such a healing comfort food and freezes so well. Highly recommend!! Thank you for sharing.

Good Polish Cabbage soup. Skip the dried onion soup mix, and just use salt, pepper, and powdered garlic and onion to taste if you think you need it. Too many recipes call for instant soup mix, its expensive, ultra processed and you can substitute real spices.

This is a good base recipe but I skip the onion soup mix and bottled tomato juice. Too much sodium. I use both Better than Bullion beef AND vegetable base (low sodium). I also add garlic, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes for a kick. Sometimes I’ll add ground turkey or chicken for extra protein. And I use fresh or frozen green beans. I love this recipe, I don’t use it for weight loss. It’s just a warm filling HEALTHY meal in winter 🥰

Delicious! I did make some changes to suit my and my family’s and friends’ tastes: • I omitted the bell peppers and tomato juice. • i used chicken broth in place of beef broth, canned chopped tomatoes in place of whole, and chopped onions to replace the onion soup mix. • i added canned corn and garbanzo beans, as well as Italian seasoning. Everyone raved about how fresh, clean, and good it tasted. Making this on repeat.
I sprinkle with a little grated parmesan and added some cayenne pepper Yummy!
I've been eating this since a child w/ my Grandma. I however add all different kinds of garden veg. & herbs on hand. I also add low fat meat like chicken or seafood for protein. So good!
Made it exactly as written - turned out to be fanastic.
I eat this soup all year long just because it is good!
It is really easy to mix and match and choose a variety of ingredients for this soup, which I love. It is also very simple to make and very healthy, but it could use more flavor.

I lost 4 lbs. the first week. I did alter the ingredients a little by adding some ground turkey and a can of white beans for protein and fiber. I did not add the onion soup mix, too much sodium. I added a large chopped onion and broth made with better than bouillon roasted beef instead of the soup. I eat a cup of it every day either for lunch or with dinner with meat or fish.
I'm a meat eater but this was a very tasteful soup which 8 of my adult relatives loved. With 0 dislikes.
Very good, but kind of on the bland side. Added a dash of salt & pepper to taste. Will definitely make again.
